idiom_name: test suite class extends the collaborator trait and passes this (SAM lambda for one-method traits)
implementation_notes: Scala test suites are classes or objects, so the collaborator trait can be mixed into the suite and this passed to the SUT, with recording in a suite field; ScalaTest creates a fresh suite instance per test, which keeps that state per-test. Scala 3 also converts a function literal to a single-abstract-method trait, so a lambda can serve as the collaborator and confine the double to one test -- an Inner Test Double rather than a Self Shunt. The trait-mixin form stays justified when the collaborator has several members or when several tests in the suite observe the same callback; mockito-scala or scalamock takes over when verification, not recording, is required.
pitfalls: Mixing a production trait into the suite forces every abstract member to be implemented there, so a wide trait bloats the suite and recompiles it whenever the trait changes.
this escapes into the SUT: a collaborator stored beyond the test can call back after the suite finished, so unregister listeners in an afterEach hook.
SAM conversion applies only to traits with exactly one abstract method; with a second abstract member the compiler demands an explicit implementation or an anonymous class instead.
